array_filter.markdown:
Filters an array by passing each item to the filter function
and keeping only the ones that it returned `true` for.

If `copy` is `true`, filtered items will be added to a new array.\
Otherwise the array is modified in place.

Returns the array (either new or the input one) in both cases.

On terms of modern GML, the function is a mix of
`array_filter` (GameMaker manual) and `array_filter_ext` (GameMaker manual).

array_find_index.markdown:
Returns the index of first occurrence of a value in the array.
```
var arr = ["a", "b", "c"];
trace(array_find_index(arr, "b")); // 1
trace(array_find_index(arr, "c")); // 2
trace(array_find_index(arr, "d")); // -1
```
This is the primary reason for the `native_` prefixes - in GML functions,
`array_find_index` uses a _predicate_ to search an array
while `array_get_index` searches for a value.
A confusing one given the names of `ds_list` functions.

array_find_index_ext.markdown: Like above, but starts searching at a specific index (inclusive).

array_find_last_index.markdown: Like above, but searches from the end of an array.

array_find_last_index_ext.markdown: Like above, but searches for values before the specified index (exclusive).

array_join.markdown:
Joins the contents of an array into a string, separating them as specified.
```
var arr = [1, 2, 3];
trace(array_join(arr, "|")); // "1|2|3"
```
`string_split` can be considered a counterpart of this function.

array_length_1d.markdown: Same thing as array_length, here for backwards compatibility.

array_map.markdown:
Modifies an array by passing all items through a mapper function.

If `copy` is `true`, resulting items will be added to a new array.\
Otherwise the array is modified in place.

Returns the array (either new or the input one) in both cases.

On terms of modern GML, the function is a mix of
`array_map` (GameMaker manual) and `array_map_ext` (GameMaker manual).

array_slice.markdown:
Returns a new array with values representing a section of an array.

This is more or less a shortcut for `array_create(length)` + `array_copy`.
```
var arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
trace(array_slice(arr, 1, 3)); // [1, 2, 3]
```

array_sort_sub.markdown:
Assuming an array of arrays,
sorts the contents based on `sub_index`-th element of each sub-array.

These days you can pass a predicate function to `array_sort`.

draw_text_nt.markdown:
Draws text with tags!
-	`@s`: Silver
-	`@d`: Dark gray
-	`@y`: Yellow
-	`@r`: Red
-	`@b`: Blue
-	`@g`: Green
-	`@p`: Purple
-	`@w`: White
-	`@q`: Cursed/shaky text
-	`@(...)`, `@0(...)`, `@9(...)`:\
	You can do `@(sprAmmo)` or `@(sprAmmo:1)` to draw sprites.

	`@0` .. `@9` indicates how much space the sprite takes up in text.

	This is also used for some special things: --{
	-	`@(keysmall:action)`:\
		Displays the current key binding for an action.

		Possible actions are: --{
		-	`fire`
		-	`spec`
		-	`pick`
		-	`swap`
		-	`nort`
		-	`sout`
		-	`east`
		-	`west`
		}
	-	`@(keysmall2:action)`:\
		Displays the alternate key binding for an action.
	-	`@(butsmall:action)`:\
		Displays the current gamepad button binding for an action.
	-	`@(butsmall2:action)`:\
		Displays the alternate gamepad button binding for an action.
	-	`@(butbig:action)`:\
		Like above, but for big buttons.
	-	`@(butbig2:action)`:\
		Like above, but for big buttons and alternate binding.
	-	`@(color:value)`:\
		Applies a custom color.

		`value` can be either a numeric BGR color in GameMaker format
		(such as from `make_color_rgb`) or a `#RrGgBb` hex.
	}
}

Also note that it accepts an indentation string

instead of a boolean flag like the built-in function does.

player_get_alias.markdown:

This is handy for displaying leaderboards or other UI that addresses the players.

player_get_race.markdown:
Returns the current character for a player slot.

These are strings like `"fish"`, `"robot"`,
or mod names for custom characters.

player_get_race_id.markdown:
Returns the current character index for a player slot.

These are numbers like 1 (or `char_fish`) for Fish,
5 (or `char_robot`) for Robot,
or `char_custom` for mods.

All mods share the race index so you'll want to use `player_get_race`
to tell modded characters apart.

player_get_uid.markdown:
Returns the numeric "unique ID" of a player controlling the slot.

If two slots have the same UID, they are being controlled from the same computer.

A player that joined the lobby earlier will have a lower UID
than a player that joined (or re-joined) the lobby later,
but otherwise no pattern is guaranteed for these,
and they can have "gaps".

player_is_local_nonsync.markdown:

sprite_get_name.markdown: Sprites added through `sprite_add` and alike will have their name set based on file name.

sprite_replace.markdown:
Similar to above, but also `xorigin` / `yorigin` arguments are now optional
in case you are replacing a sprite with a same-sized one.

sprite_replace_image.markdown: Replaces a single subimage of a sprite. A convenience function.

sprite_restore.markdown:
Undoes whatever changes made by `sprite_replace` and alike.

Returns whether there was anything to undo.

string_auto.markdown:
Converts a number to a string with automatic precision
(unlike `string_format`, which requires specifying the number of decimal places).
```
trace(string_auto(0.4)); // "0.4"
trace(string_auto(0.4040)); // "0.404"
```

string_is_real.markdown:
Returns whether a string contains a valid number
(signed, fractional, no exponents/infinities).

string_lpad.markdown:
Prepends `padstr` to `str` until it reaches specified length.
```
trace(string_lpad(string(42), "0", 4)); // "0042"
```

string_ltrim.markdown:
Removes leading spaces from a string.
```
trace(string_trim(" hi ")); // "hi "
```
Same as now-built-in `string_trim_start`.

string_md5.markdown: Returns a MD5 hash of a string, assuming Unicode encoding.

string_md5_utf8.markdown: Returns a MD5 hash of a string, assuming UTF-8 encoding.

string_rpad.markdown:
Appends `padstr` to `str` until it reaches specified length.
```
trace(string_rpad(string(42), "0", 4)); // "4200"
```

string_rtrim.markdown:
Removes trailing spaces from a string.
```
trace(string_trim(" hi ")); // " hi"
```
Same as now-built-in `string_trim_end`.

string_sha1.markdown: Returns a SHA-1 hash of a string, assuming Unicode encoding.

string_sha1_utf8.markdown: Returns a SHA-1 hash of a string, assuming UTF-8 encoding.

string_split_list.markdown:
Splits a string on delimiter into an list of strings.

If `list` is provided, clears it and adds items to it, otherwise makes a new list.

Returns the list.

If the string does not contain the delimiter, returns a 1-element array with the entire string.
```
var list = string_split_list("A|B|C", "|");
trace(list[|1]); // "B"
```

string_to_real.markdown:
Converts a string to a number if it's valid (rules per above)
or returns `default_value` if it isn't.

In "legacy" NTGML, `real(str)` is equivalent
to `string_to_real(str, 0)` for backwards compatibility.

string_trim.markdown:
Removes leading and trailing spaces from a string.
```
trace(string_trim(" hi ")); // "hi"
```
Same as now-built-in `string_trim`.

surface_destroy_soft.markdown:
Like regular `surface_destroy`, but does not throw an error if you try to destroy a non-existing
surface.

This is what "legacy" mods use instead of `surface_destroy`.

surface_screenshot.markdown: Takes a screenshot to a surface.

surface_valid.markdown: Same thing as with data structure checkers.

trace.markdown:
Displays the given value(s) in chat.

A local alternative to GM's `show_debug_message`.

Values are separated by a single space.

Non-string values are converted to string prior.
```
trace(1, 2); // "1 2"
trace(room_speed, "FPS"); // "60 FPS"
var arr = [1,2,3];
trace(arr); // "[1, 2, 3]"
var obj = {a:1,b:2};
trace(obj); // "{ a: 1, b: 2 }"
```
Advanced users can also enable this function to log to standard output
using the `/stdout` chat command - this allows to get back values even if the game does
not survive until the next screen redraw.

typeof.markdown:
Returns the type of a value as a string.

This is slower than calling the respective `is_` function or two.

variable_instance_get.markdown:
Same as original, but you can provide the default value
if the variable isn't in the instance.

weapon_get_area.markdown:
Returns the difficulty tier that determines when the weapon should start dropping.

Tier of `-1` means that a weapon doesn't drop "naturally".

weapon_get_auto.markdown: Returns whether a weapon is automatic.

weapon_get_cost.markdown: Returns the weapon's ammo cost per shot.

weapon_get_gold.markdown: Returns whether a weapon is a gold weapon.

weapon_get_laser_sight.markdown:
Returns whether a weapon should display a laser sight.

By default, only bolt weapons (except for Disc Gun) do.

weapon_get_load.markdown: Returns reload time of the given weapon (in frames at 30fps).

weapon_get_name.markdown: Returns display name of a weapon.

weapon_get_rads.markdown: Returns the weapon's rad cost per shot.

weapon_get_sprite.markdown:
Returns the sprite for the given weapon.

`weapon_get_sprt` is an alias for this function.

weapon_get_sprite_hud.markdown:
Returns the HUD sprite of a weapon.

`weapon_get_sprt_hud` is an alias for this function.

There is no setter function for this one because only modded weapons
can have a separate HUD sprite.

weapon_get_swap.markdown: Returns the sound that plays when a weapon is swapped to.

weapon_get_text.markdown: Returns a weapon's loading screen tooltip.

weapon_get_type.markdown:
Returns the ammo type of a weapon.
Types are as following:

```table
Index | Type
0 | Melee / no ammo
1 | Bullet
2 | Shotgun
3 | Bolt
4 | Explosive
5 | Laser
```

weapon_is_melee.markdown:
Returns whether a weapon is a melee weapon.

Melee weapons are held to a side and flip on swing.

weapon_set_area.markdown:
Changes the difficulty tier of a weapon.

If you are making a mod that replaces built-in weapon(s),
setting their tier to `-1` is a good way to prevent the original weapons from dropping.

weapon_set_auto.markdown: Changes whether a weapon is automatic.

weapon_set_cost.markdown: Changes a weapon's ammo cost per shot.

weapon_set_load.markdown:
Changes reload time of a weapon (in frames at 30fps).

If reload time is less than 1 frame at the current framerate,
multiple projectiles may be shot per frame.

weapon_set_name.markdown: Changes display name of a weapon.

weapon_set_rads.markdown: Changes a weapon's rad cost per shot.

weapon_set_swap.markdown: Changes the sound that plays when a weapon is swapped to.

weapon_set_text.markdown: Changes a weapon's loading screen tooltip.

weapon_set_type.markdown: Changes ammo type of a weapon.
